title: Show a revoked or expired counterparty pin as no longer paired
body:
## Summary
counterparty_list reads neither revoked_at nor expires_at, so a pin the owner revoked (or that lapsed) still lists as words-confirmed / house-pinned with its name.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/display.rs:16-19 selects key_id, display_name, paired_via, first_seen, words_confirmed_at, declared_payee only; pairing is derived from words_confirmed_at alone (:33-37). crates/table-ledger/src/pin.rs:22-35 is the only reader of revoked_at/expires_at and the gate refuses such a pin (require_live), so every money path treats it as unpaired while the owner's list says paired. Production revoke exists: crates/table-runtime/src/dispatcher.rs:577 (IPC counterparty_revoke). CounterpartyPairing (crates/table-core/src/display.rs:55) has no revoked/expired variant, so the fix crosses table-core, bindings and the client.

## Flow
- owner revokes a counterparty in the approval window (counterparty_revoke)
- main window lists counterparties (dispatcher.rs:205 -> counterparty_list)
- observed: pairing words_confirmed, name shown, as before the revoke
- fix: counterparty_list takes now, reads pin::state per row and projects a Revoked/Expired pairing (new enum variants, regenerated bindings, client copy)

## Expected impact
The owner sees the state the gate already enforces; today the list contradicts every refusal the pin produces. Could break client code that exhaustively matches CounterpartyPairing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the counterparty list says what the pin gate decides
Before: a revoked pin lists as words_confirmed (walked: pin.rs revoke path + display.rs:33-37)
After: the same pin lists as revoked; an expired one as expired
Method: simulation - revoke then list walked through display.rs; the gate run needs a table-core enum change outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: table-ledger test: pin a counterparty, revoke_counterparty, counterparty_list -> assert pairing is not WordsConfirmed (red today); plus an expires_at in the past case

title: Say when a Book answer was cut at its row limit
body:
## Summary
book_query returns at most `limit` grouped rows with no signal that more existed, and reports max_rows:500 whatever limit the query set, so a truncated answer reads as complete.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:181 binds LIMIT query.limit.unwrap_or(500); :244-246 returns {rows, amount_units, market_units, max_rows:500}. A query grouped by counterparty or day over more groups than the limit drops the tail silently; a limit of 50 still claims max_rows 500. audit_page/history_rows in the same crate fetch limit+1 and return `more` (crates/table-ledger/src/audit.rs) - the pattern exists. The answer reaches the owner's Book and the agent (crates/table-app/src/agent.rs:571).

## Flow
- owner asks the Book for sums by counterparty over a ledger with more counterparties than the limit
- book.rs compiles LIMIT ? and returns the first N groups
- observed: the answer has no truncation flag; totals read as the whole book
- fix: fetch limit+1, return truncated: bool and the effective limit; client Book shows 'first N of more'

## Expected impact
A partial answer stops passing for a complete one in the Book and in what the agent reads. Additive field; the mock backend and client model need the same field.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a cut answer is distinguishable from a complete one
Before: 0 of 2 truncation signals (no flag; max_rows constant 500 even for limit 50)
After: truncated flag true exactly when a row beyond the limit exists; max_rows = effective limit
Method: simulation - book.rs:181,244 read; a gate needs the client/mock contract changed outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: table-ledger test: insert 3 deals with distinct counterparties, book_query group_by counterparty limit 2 -> assert a truncated flag (red today: field absent) and max_rows == 2

title: Leave a trace when a relay reset or an inbox overflow is refused
body:
## Summary
stage_relay_batch refuses a second generation reset inside RESET_WINDOW_SECS and an inbox past INBOX_CAP with a bare Conflict and no audit row, so a relay that keeps resetting a deal leaves nothing an owner or auditor can see.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/relay.rs:292-294 (reset inside 600 s) and :319-321 (held > 1024) return Conflict before any write; the comments call these backstops against a misbehaving relay. Every other relay refusal of content is recorded (reject_inbox, :401-449, envelope.rejected). A refused reset is retried each poll, so a naive row per refusal would flood the chain - the fix needs one row per (deal, refused generation).

## Flow
- relay restarts a deal's generation twice in ten minutes
- stage_relay_batch refuses the second (relay.rs:292)
- observed: audit_count unchanged; the deal silently stalls until the window passes
- fix: append relay.reset_refused {generation, reason} once per (deal, generation), allowlisted, classified as bookkeeping in runtime history

## Expected impact
An abusive or broken relay becomes visible in the safety record. Could add chain rows on every poll if the dedupe is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a refused relay behaviour leaves evidence
Before: 2 refusal paths with 0 audit rows (relay.rs:292,319)
After: 2 of 2 leave one row per (deal, generation)
Method: simulation - read; the instrument is a ledger test and the runtime classifier list is outside this round
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: table-ledger test: bind a route, stage gen A, stage gen B, stage gen C at +10 s -> Conflict and assert one relay.reset_refused row (red today: 0); a second refused attempt for C adds none

title: Check paypal_calls metadata on both of its writers
body:
## Summary
Two functions insert paypal_calls rows; record_paypal_call validates request_id charset/length and refuses request_id or path containing a sensitive value, insert_calls (the money-step path) validates neither and redacts with no sensitive values.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/countersign.rs:261-271 refuses request_id >128, outside [A-Za-z0-9-_], or containing a sensitive value; crates/table-ledger/src/repositories.rs:132-147 (insert_calls, used by finish_operation and resolution) checks only deal_id and calls redact_paypal(&call.response, &[]). One rule, two writers, 1 of 2 enforce it. Refusing an evidence write after a money call already happened is itself risky (the transaction rolls back the operation status), so the fix should redact/normalize rather than refuse on that path - a design choice for the worker.

## Flow
- pipeline finishes a capture with a PaypalCall whose request_id carries an unexpected character
- finish_operation -> insert_calls stores it unchecked
- record_paypal_call would have refused the same row

## Expected impact
Stored call metadata obeys one rule whichever path wrote it. Risk: a refusal on the money path loses the observed outcome - hence redact, not refuse.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one metadata rule for every paypal_calls writer
Before: 1 of 2 writers check request_id/path
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read both writers; the decision refuse-vs-redact on the post-money path needs the worker's test
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: table-ledger test: finish_operation with a call whose request_id is 'a b' -> stored verbatim today (red); after: stored redacted/normalized and the operation still confirmed

title: Declare time once in the workspace and drop the ledger's unused formatting feature
body:
## Summary
time is declared per crate (table-ledger and table-paypal, identical lines) outside [workspace.dependencies], and table-ledger enables the formatting feature it never uses.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/Cargo.toml:10 time = {version="0.3",features=["formatting","parsing"]}; the crate's only use is OffsetDateTime::parse with Rfc3339 (crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:61). crates/table-paypal/Cargo.toml:13 repeats the line. Every other shared dependency is a workspace entry. Cargo.toml files are outside this round's declared paths.

## Flow
- grep time:: in crates/table-ledger/src -> 1 site, parse only
- move time to [workspace.dependencies]; ledger takes parsing, paypal what it uses

## Expected impact
One version line for time; the ledger's standalone build compiles less. Nothing behavioural.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - declared features match use; one version source
Before: 2 per-crate declarations; 1 unused feature in table-ledger
After: 1 workspace declaration; 0 unused
Method: probe - grep of time:: uses (1 site, parsing only)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: cargo tree -p table-ledger -e features shows time feature formatting before, not after; cargo build -p table-ledger and -p table-paypal green

title: Decide a horizon for nonces_seen, whose exp is written and never read
body:
## Summary
Every stored envelope inserts a nonces_seen row with exp, nothing ever reads exp or deletes a row, and the nonce_expiry index is maintained for no query.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:31 and 0002_integrity.sql:7 (CREATE INDEX nonce_expiry ON nonces_seen(exp)); writer crates/table-ledger/src/negotiation.rs:146-149, reader negotiation.rs:17-24 (key_id, nonce only). verify_transcript replays with in-memory nonces (crates/table-ledger/src/transcript.rs), and verify() refuses an expired envelope, so a nonce past exp cannot be replayed anyway. Pruning deletes stored rows from the replay-protection table, which is an owner decision.

## Flow
- each OFFER/COUNTER/ACCEPT/SETTLE/RECEIPT/NOTE adds one row forever
- index nonce_expiry is updated on every insert and used by no query

## Expected impact
Bounded growth of a table that grows with every message; or, if kept, a dropped index and a stated reason.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the store states a horizon for replay nonces
Before: 1 column + 1 index written, 0 readers; 0 deletes
After: a stated horizon (prune past exp + skew) or the index dropped
Method: probe - grep of nonces_seen readers/writers (2 statements)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
instrument: count nonces_seen rows vs envelopes rows on a long-lived ledger copy; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN of the two nonce statements (nonce_expiry unused)

title: Retire schema states nothing writes: deals_closed, mandate 'expired', mandate kinds
body:
## Summary
The schema admits states no code reaches: counterparties.deals_closed is never written (always 0) because the list computes the count; mandates.status 'expired' is never set; mandates.kind 'rescue'/'shop' are never written (insert hard-codes 'open').

## Description
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:13 deals_closed INTEGER DEFAULT 0 - no writer anywhere (grep), crates/table-ledger/src/display.rs:17 computes it from deals. 0001_table.sql:6 status CHECK includes 'expired'; writers set only 'superseded' and 'revoked' (crates/table-ledger/src/mandates.rs:168,211); expiry is judged on read. 0001_table.sql:2 kind CHECK ('open','rescue','shop'); crates/table-ledger/src/mandates.rs:171 inserts 'open' always. A reader that trusts these columns reads a value that is always the default.

## Flow
- grep deals_closed writers -> 0; grep status='expired' writers -> 0; grep kind values written -> 'open' only

## Expected impact
The schema stops promising states that never occur; any change is a migration on the merchant's single store.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every admitted state has a writer or is gone
Before: 3 admitted states/columns with 0 writers
After: 0
Method: probe - greps over crates/ for each writer
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
instrument: a schema test listing each CHECK value and asserting a production writer exists (grep-derived), seeded red by the three above

title: Correct 0001's column comments, pinned verbatim to the design report
body:
## Summary
0001_table.sql's comments describe shapes the code never writes, and the file is pinned verbatim to docs/design/the-table.html, so the fix is a design-report edit plus a migration-file edit.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:22 decided_by -- 'policy:clause6' | 'human:2026-..' (code writes canonical DecidedBy JSON; crates/table-ledger/src/repositories.rs:124-128 says so); :43 actor -- 'agent:buyer-1' | 'owner' | 'policy:clause6' | 'peer:47be..' (writers use 'policy', 'agent', 'pipeline', 'attention', 'house-witness', ...); :20 market_json -- Channel3 snapshot (a MarketRef). crates/table-ledger/src/tests.rs migration_0001_matches_report_html_verbatim compares the file to the report, so editing either alone goes red; editing an applied migration is a change to shipped schema text.

## Flow
- read 0001 comments against the writers named

## Expected impact
A reader of the DDL learns the real shapes; the report and the file move together.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stated column shapes match the writers
Before: 3 comments describing unwritten shapes
After: 0
Method: probe - each comment checked against its writers
Result: better
Gate: irreversible
instrument: migration_0001_matches_report_html_verbatim stays green with report and file edited together

title: Unify the two redaction markers ([REDACTED] vs [redacted])
body:
## Summary
redaction.rs writes [REDACTED] into paypal_calls bodies and audit_detail.rs writes [redacted] into audit details.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/redaction.rs:50 (paypal body marker) vs crates/table-ledger/src/audit_detail.rs:23. Rows already stored keep their marker forever (audit_log is append-only and hash-chained), so changing either constant leaves both spellings in the store.

## Flow
- count markers a reader must know: 2 before, 2 after (old rows keep theirs)

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one redaction marker
Before: 2 markers in the store
After: 2 markers in the store (stored rows are immutable)
Method: probe - the stored-row constraint read
Result: not-better
Gate: none
